metadata.case_name: OU JIANPING v. HONG KONG HOUSING AUTHORITY

plaintiff.occupation_before: housewife; previously worked as a security guard (temporary), home helper and a kitchen worker

injuries.description: severe injury to her left knee
source: As a result of the accident, the plaintiff sustained severe injury to her left knee.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the knee or lower leg, unspecified

injuries.description: pre-existing poliomyelitis of the left lower limb resulting in pre-existing weakness, limb discrepancy and ankle deformity
source: In the present case, there is no dispute between Dr Wong and Dr Lee that theplaintiff had pre-existing poliomyelitis.

Dr Lee opines that the pre-existing weakness and shortening of the plaintiff's left limb was due to poliomyelitis. The muscle weakness, limb discrepancy and ankle deformity are the result of the pre-existing poliomyelitis.
Dr Wong opines that the poliomyelitis of the left lower limb largely accounts for the chronic muscle disuse and leg discrepancy of her left lower limb.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the ankle or foot

manifestations.description: knee bumped against the metal cover of the ditch
5 scars from surgery in China in 1990 while she had 2 scars from the surgery after the accident
The CT scan taken on 8 April 2010 show osteopenia and muscle atrophy indicating chronic disuse.
would walk less stable than an ordinary person

treatments_received: 14-days stay at the Tuen Mun Hospital
surgery after the accident (resulting in 2 scars)
periodic consultations at the Tuen Mun Hospital
treatments_future: operation to remove the metal implant in her left leg (Dr Wong suggests; cost around HK$30,000 to HK$40,000 if performed in the private sector)
the best institute to carry out the operation will be the Tuen Mun Hospital (as stated in judgment)
